title: Security review - encryption & KMS/BYOK/HSM
summary: Helios Bank security team reviewed Redwood's encryption model and key management options. Discussion covered default encryption at rest/ in transit, BYOK workflows, HSM requirements, audit logging, and performance implications for dedicated vs hosted deployments. Action items: share attestations and KMS integration guide, follow-up pilot for BYOK performance testing.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestations and encryption whitepaper
Send KMS/BYOK implementation guide and HSM option matrix
Schedule 2-hour pilot run to benchmark encryption performance (redwood + helios keys)
Follow up on contractual BYOK clause and SLAs
action_items: Maya Patel - Send SOC 2 and ISO certs and encryption whitepaper - 2026-06-14
Ethan Chen - Prepare KMS/BYOK implementation guide + HSM option matrix - 2026-06-16
Liam O'Connor - Provide list of Helios-approved HSM vendors and compliance constraints - 2026-06-15
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Ethan is our SE, we'll run through encryption and key management questions.
[00:10] Sofia (Helios - CISO): Thanks, Maya. We just want to make sure we cover encryption at rest and in transit, BYOK, and whether Redwood supports HSM backed keys for our regulatory needs.
[00:22] Ethan (Redwood SE): Absolutely. Quick agenda — high level architecture, default encryption, KMS integrations, BYOK flow, HSM options (CloudHSM/Thales), audit logs and rotation. Happy to dig into any area.
[00:35] Priya (Helios - Dir Security): Our baseline is SOC 2 + ISO 27001, and anything touching keys needs to be FIPS validated for at-rest key storage. We also have data residency constraints — some tokens must stay in EU regions.
[00:48] Maya: Got it. To start, Redwood encrypts data in transit with TLS 1.2/1.3 by default; mutual TLS is available for dedicated/private deployments. For at-rest we use envelope encryption: customer payloads are encrypted with per-tenant data keys which are themselves wrapped by a root key managed in a KMS.
[01:05] Liam (Helios - Head of Platform): When you say "KMS", you mean Redwood's managed KMS or can we supply our own? We require BYOK for production.
[01:13] Ethan: You can definitely bring your own keys. We support BYOK workflows where the customer holds the root key in their cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) or a customer-managed HSM like Thales or CloudHSM. In that flow, Redwood performs key wrapping/unwrapping calls to your KMS — Redwood never persists the unwrapped root key.
[01:33] Sofia: And what about HSM? We need HSM-stored root keys with no exportability and tamper-proof hardware.
[01:39] Ethan: Yep. For HSM-backed keys we support two modes: 1) Customer-managed Cloud HSM where your KMS is backed by an HSM (e.g., AWS CloudHSM + AWS KMS in a custom key store), or 2) On-premise HSM bridged to a customer KMS via a gateway. In both cases, key operations are performed by the KMS/HSM; Redwood gets an encrypted key blob or performs envelope calls — we never receive plaintext root keys.
[01:59] Priya: Good. Can you walk through the BYOK key rotation and compromise scenarios? We need a clear playbook for rotation and emergency key rotation.
[02:07] Ethan: Sure. Standard flow: you rotate the root key in your KMS on your schedule. Redwood supports re-wrapping the per-tenant data keys with the new root. We also support key versioning — each wrapped key includes metadata for the KMS key version. In a compromise, you can immediately revoke the root key in your KMS; that will prevent Redwood from unwrapping new data keys. For active incidents we recommend the dedicated deployment so you can isolate, but we can also help with rekeying and data re-encryption jobs.
[02:32] Maya: Important to note: for hosted customers who don't choose BYOK, Redwood manages the root keys in our HSM-backed KMS and we provide attestations, regular rotation, and access controls. For BYOK we provide integration docs and an onboarding checklist.
[02:45] Liam: How about audit logs? We need cryptographic proof of key usage and detailed logs for every unwrap/wrap operation for audits.
[02:53] Ethan: We produce audit logs for all key operations: API calls to wrap/unwrap, timestamps, requesting principal, and the activity is retained in our audit log store. For enterprise customers we can push log export to your SIEM or S3 bucket and integrate with your log retention policies. Logs include request IDs and are correlated with request traces in the Redwood Console.
[03:12] Sofia: Retention length? We need seven years for certain data access logs.
[03:16] Maya: We have configurable retention for audit logs in the enterprise package; default is 90 days, but we offer extended retention add-ons up to multi-year retention and can export to your archive store for regulatory retention windows.
[03:28] Priya: Performance impact — do we see latency increases when using BYOK or HSM? Our SLAs are sensitive; we run low-latency payments fraud models.
[03:36] Ethan: There's modest overhead at key unwrap/wrap time. Envelope encryption ensures per-request tokenization/decryption rarely hits the root key; typically the per-tenant data key is cached in an encrypted KV and rotated periodically. For streaming inference, the critical path is symmetric crypto (AES-GCM) which is very fast. HSM operations (asymmetric ops) are slower and we minimize them to key operations (e.g., key wrap/unwrapping) rather than per-token crypto, so runtime latency impact is usually in low tens of milliseconds for the unwrap, and that is often amortized. For dedicated pods we can provision local caches and keep KV caches warm to reduce unwrap frequency.
[04:08] Liam: You mentioned KV cache — is that the same as KV cache for model inference or a key-value store for wrapped keys?
[04:14] Ethan: Sorry, overloaded term. I meant our key vault cache — we keep wrapped data keys cached in a secure enclave/keystore to avoid hitting KMS on every request. For model KV cache (attention KV cache) that's different.
[04:25] Priya: What's the attack surface for the cache? If an attacker compromises a compute node, can they get the plaintext data keys?
[04:31] Ethan: We protect caches with process-level encryption and strict OS-level controls. On Redwood-managed hosted, we use hardware protections and compartmentalization — plaintext keys are only in memory for a short time, and we scrub on process exit. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can enable stricter controls, e.g., only allow ephemeral unwrapping on a sealed enclave or use customer side key wrapping.
[04:50] Sofia: For our auditors, we need FIPS 140-2/3 validated paths and Crypto-agility documented. Do you have FIPS attestations?
[04:58] Maya: Redwood's managed KMS is FIPS-compliant and our HSM partners provide FIPS validated modules. We will share the specific certificates and our crypto whitepaper, showing the validated paths.
[05:08] Liam: Any regional limitations? Our EU data must never leave eu-west-1.
[05:13] Ethan: We support region pinning — you can pin data to a region. For BYOK you can provision your KMS key in the EU region, and Redwood will keep wrapped keys and data in that region when you choose an EU-only deployment. We'll include the regional deployment checklist in the doc pack.
[05:27] Priya: Contractually, we need a BYOK clause that states Redwood will never export or persist customer plaintext keys and will comply with key custody specs.
[05:36] Maya: We already have contractual language used with other banks; we'll provide a BYOK clause template and can iterate for legal.
[05:42] Sofia: About TLS — mutual TLS for inbound calls, is that supported for hosted or only dedicated/private?
[05:48] Ethan: Mutual TLS is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we support client TLS and token-based auth; we also support SAML/SSO for admin access and RBAC. For a bank with tight network controls, Dedicated or Private usually fits better.
[06:02] Liam: Regarding RBAC and SSO — can we map our IdP groups to Redwood roles and enforce least privilege?
[06:08] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning is supported; you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles and enforce MFA via your IdP. We also support fine-grained RBAC at the route/model level for administrators, operators, and viewers.
[06:21] Priya: Auditability of admin actions — we need to show who changed rollout policies or model pinning.
[06:27] Ethan: All console actions are audited with user identities and timestamps; you can export these to your SIEM. We also have immutable trails for rollout changes tied to request IDs.
[06:38] Sofia: Any limitations around tokenization and PII — can we bring pre-tokenized data, or must you process raw PII?
[06:46] Ethan: You can supply pre-tokenized data; our API accepts opaque tokens or raw strings. For tokens we treat them as opaque bytes and encrypt them at rest. For really sensitive PII, we recommend processing in a Private deployment with customer-managed keys.
[06:58] Liam: Let's talk about backup encryption. If Redwood stores backups of customer data, how are those encrypted and who manages keys?
[07:06] Maya: Backups are encrypted with the same envelope approach. For BYOK customers, the backup snapshots are encrypted with the tenant data key and wrapped by your root key. For hosted customers, Redwood manages root keys but we can provide proof of encryption and key handling logs.
[07:18] Priya: Can we do periodic rekeying of backups independently of live data keys? Our policy requires rotating backup wrap keys quarterly.
[07:25] Ethan: Yes. We support separate rotation schedules for backup wrap keys and live data keys. We'll include instructions on how to trigger rewrap jobs via the API.
[07:34] Sofia: Pen testing — do you allow key-rotation/drill tests where we simulate compromise and verify rekey/recovery?
[07:41] Maya: Yes, we do war-room/incident drills with enterprise customers. We can schedule a simulated rotation and rekeying exercise; we also provide pre-approved runbooks.
[07:50] Liam: Compliance packages — we need SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certs, and encryption whitepapers.
[07:56] Maya: We'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs as well as a KMS/HSM whitepaper and the BYOK checklist. Expect an email with links by EOD Friday.
[08:06] Priya: One more: Do you support customer-provided HSMs in our own DC with a gateway to Redwood private deployment? We have legacy HSMs in-house.
[08:13] Ethan: For Private deployments we can integrate with on-prem HSMs via a secure gateway. That requires additional engineering but we've done it before; we'll capture the architecture pattern in the follow-up doc.
[08:24] Sofia: Great. For the pilot, what's the minimal scope? We want to measure unwrap latency and overall throughput when using our KMS.
[08:32] Ethan: Minimal pilot: 1-2 dedicated pods in Helios region, your KMS key provisioned, a 2-hour synthetic benchmark with varied sequence lengths and token rates. We'll capture tail latency and unwrap counts. We'll provide scripts and a results dashboard.
[08:45] Liam: Cost impact? HSM usage costs are a concern.
[08:48] Maya: We'll provide a cost estimate comparing Redwood-managed keys vs BYOK on AWS KMS + CloudHSM charges and the amortized HSM call costs per 1M requests.
[08:58] Priya: For my auditors, can you provide cryptographic algorithm lists and parameters (e.g., AES-GCM-256, RSA-2048/3072 usage only for wrap)?
[09:06] Ethan: Yes, we use AES-256-GCM for symmetric data encryption, RSA or ECC for key wrapping depending on the KMS, and HKDF-based derivation for per-tenant keys. We'll include the algorithm suite in the whitepaper.
[09:19] Maya: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO certs, the KMS/BYOK guide, HSM option matrix, and the pilot plan. Ethan will own the technical docs; I'll own the compliance pack and contract language.
[09:33] Sofia: Sounds good. One ask — include explicit statement that Redwood will not export customer plaintext keys and will honor our key revocation.
[09:41] Maya: Understood. We'll include explicit BYOK contractual language and a sample SLA.
[09:45] Liam: Thanks all. We'll review and get you the vendor HSM list and any additional compliance constraints.
[09:50] Priya: Thanks, this was helpful.
[09:53] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the docs and schedule the pilot.
[09:58] End of transcript (approx)
